report.experience: Clear and brief, more like configuring a small constitution than discovering combinations. The initial rules gave enough information to choose a six-action route without guessing.
report.worthDoing: Separating personal authority from the existing common garden voice was the meaningful choice. Sharing memories then had a visible practical consequence: the garden revision was accepted without changing personal consent.
report.keep: Keep exact public rules, actual actor responses, scope-specific authority, and permission to leave Mara as caretaker. These let a simple solution remain legitimate.
report.shorten: Shorten the repeated world dump on discovery-only actions, and consider collapsing the template-plus-scope construction into one operation; those intermediate actions did not add much decision-making for me.
report.removeOrChange: Show effective authority alongside explicit authority: garden null can look unauthorized even though the inherited common voice is valid. No branch needs removal on the evidence of this short route, but I had no reason to explore merger or care transfer after solving the goals.
report.stoppingReason: All three public goals hold after six accepted combinations. Further branching would not serve the assigned outcome.

report.question: What, if anything, did the future-personhood setting add to or detract from your experience?
report.answer: It gave a concrete reason to distinguish shared memories, shared civic identity and independent consent: copying a life need not copy its promises or let one voice decide everything. The two new memories also made reunion useful without requiring a merger. On my short route, though, the actual problem felt mostly like an ordinary scoped-authority arrangement between relatives; I did not need to engage deeply with future personhood. The setting added an intelligible premise and some thematic interest, but the named philosophical combinations and extensive exposition were more elaborate than the six-action configuration required.

final.title: A Promise With Two Futures

goals.text: Keep the garden accessible under a valid caretaker while Lio joins the expedition by individual consent, without inheriting Mara’s promise merely through copying.
Let both relatives use both new memories while each actually refuses the unrelated survey in their own right.
Accept the residents’ revised garden plan through an authorized shared garden voice, while expedition and survey decisions remain individually authorized.
